title: people-ops
text:
people-ops

isabel_pm: Hi team — my kid turns 26 on 2026-09-30 but will be a full-time grad student abroad (UK) starting 2026-10-01. I want to keep them on benefits through school. What proof do you need and how does open enrollment factor in? Don’t want a lapse during term start.

benefits-bot: Reminder: dependent aging out is usually at 26. Exceptions for full-time students accepted with documentation. Upload under QLE or OE depending on timing. Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle

tess_benefits: Hi @isabel_pm — if the child is still a full-time student at age 26, many carriers allow extension. We need: current full-time enrollment letter from the university (on school letterhead, start date 10/01/2026), copy of passport showing residency abroad, and a signed affidavit of student status from you. Upload within 60 days of the event (date of birth).

isabel_pm: Enrollment letter will show UK term start 10/01. If OE is earlier in Oct, do I submit now or treat as a QLE at birthday?

tess_benefits: Submit as a QLE tied to the birthday (2026-09-30) with effective continuity to 10/01. If OE opens before your QLE is approved, choose "Add dependent (pending docs)" in OE and then submit the student docs ASAP. We’ll mark as pending with carrier notes.

jorge_payroll: Payroll note: premiums stop on the day before the event unless we receive approval to continue. If docs are approved, we’ll retro-adjust premiums so there’s no gap. Example: if your pay period 9/16-9/30 had premiums for 10/01+, we treat the effective date as 10/01 and adjust any overlap with code BEN-STUD-EXT. Provide employee ID and QLE number for processing.

isabel_pm: Will there be any tax implications for covering a foreign student dependent? Also, what about FSA dependent care — obviously not applicable but want to check.

leah_compliance: Generally, medical coverage for a dependent student is not taxable. However, local UK benefits/coverage rules don’t apply here; carrier treats insured as usual. FSA dependent care eligibility won’t apply for an adult dependent. If you have commuter or other benefits, check plan docs.

isabel_pm: If carrier denies extension (some carriers stricter), is COBRA available instead?

tess_benefits: COBRA is only for qualifying events on group coverage where dependent loses eligibility; it might be offered by the plan if they age out. COBRA would be billed directly to the dependent (or you) and is typically more expensive. We’ll attempt carrier extension first; if denied we’ll issue COBRA notice and give you timelines.

benefits-bot: Upload docs: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle -> select "Dependent Full-time Student at age 26" and attach enrollment letter + passport + signed affidavit.

isabel_pm: Uploading enrollment letter tonight. Thank you — want to avoid any coverage gaps as they relocate.

jorge_payroll: Once benefits approves we’ll sync premium adjustments within 2 pay cycles. If you need faster action, mark as urgent in the QLE form.

tess_benefits: Case opened: STU-2026-3301. I’ll DM you the case link and list of acceptable school letter wording.

isabel_pm: Appreciate it! :relieved:
